name: Sovereign ERP
tagline: A ledger and period-close kernel whose rules are checked by model checking and formal specifications.

highlights.title: Period close as a checked state machine
highlights.text: The Period Controller decides close, reopen and adjustment moves, and its invariants are checked against a TLA+ specification in lockstep.

highlights.title: An engine-neutral ledger
highlights.text: A Ledger Port interface with a conformance suite that any ledger engine adapter has to pass.

highlights.title: Seeded defects are caught
highlights.text: Deliberately broken variants are run against the checks, and each one is caught with its shortest counterexample.

verifyIt: Run the workspace tests and read the counts: the controller and the TLA+ transcription agree on every reachable state, and each seeded defect is caught with its shortest counterexample.

demo.title: Close a period
demo.summary: Drive the Period Controller and see the invariants refuse illegal moves. The in-browser demo is planned; this page shows a labeled placeholder until it ships.
demo.sample: a small ledger and period calendar

status: Walking skeleton: period controller and ledger port, model-checked

buildFromSource.title: Run from source
buildFromSource.intro: Sovereign ERP is a walking skeleton, so there is no binary to download. Run its checks.
buildFromSource.steps:
git clone https://github.com/intellica-ai-llc/Sovereign-ERP
cd Sovereign-ERP/code
cargo test --workspace
buildFromSource.note: Needs Rust. In a Codespace, if cargo is missing, run Codespaces: Rebuild Container.

faq.q: Can I run an ERP with this today?
faq.a: No. The repository is a walking skeleton: the Period Controller and the Ledger Port, checked against formal specifications. There is no production code yet.

faq.q: How do I check the formal results myself?
faq.a: Run TLC on formal/PeriodClose.tla and formal/Ledger.tla and compile the Lean files. These were not re-run outside the author's environment, so they are the independent check.

faq.q: cargo is not found in my Codespace.
faq.a: Run Codespaces: Rebuild Container from the Command Palette.
